visual_features.color: brownish-grey to dark brown upper body, lighter brown underparts, dark crown cap
visual_features.body_shape: sturdy macaque with short stumpy tail, powerful build
visual_features.distinctive_marks: short kinked tail carried half-erect, dark crown patch (cap) on top of head, prominent cheek whiskers
visual_features.pattern: uniform brown with darker cap on crown

description: The southern pig-tailed macaque, also known as the Sunda or Sundaland pig-tailed macaque, is a medium-sized macaque native to southern Thailand, Malaysia, Sumatra, Borneo, and Bangka Island in Indonesia. These diurnal primates are highly social, living in multi-male, multi-female groups of 9–80 individuals led by an adult dominant female. They are skilled climbers, utilizing both terrestrial and arboreal environments, and unlike almost all primates, they are known to enjoy water. As omnivores with trichromatic vision, their diverse diet consists primarily of fruits, seeds, berries, cereals, and fungi, but they also opportunistically consume invertebrates. They play a crucial role as seed dispersers, particularly for rattan species. The species has been trained for over 400 years in Thailand to harvest coconuts.
population_estimate: Population has declined by more than 50% over the last 33 years due to habitat loss, conversion of rainforest to oil palm plantations, and hunting. Exact population numbers are not well quantified across the range, but the species has disappeared from large parts of its historic range.
habitat: Lowland primary and secondary forests, coastal forests, swampy areas, and montane forests up to 1,900 m elevation. Highest densities are found in lowland and hill dipterocarp rainforests. They prefer drier, forested areas at the base of hills and slopes, but also occur near agricultural areas, oil palm plantations, and on the edges of urban environments.
threats: Habitat loss due to deforestation and conversion to oil palm plantations
Human-wildlife conflict through crop-raiding (averaging 298 complaints annually in Malaysia)
Illegal hunting, trapping, and trade for pets and biomedical research
Exposure to predators and heightened stress levels from habitat disturbance
ecosystem_role: Southern pig-tailed macaques play crucial roles as key seed dispersers, consuming fruits and seeds throughout their environment and dispersing them through defecation, dropping, or spitting. A study in peninsular Malaysia found them to be the primary, and perhaps only, seed dispersers of certain rattan species. They also act as natural pest controllers on oil palm plantations where they hunt rats and consume insects, reducing the need for chemical pesticides.
human_connection: These macaques have complex relationships with humans. Since the 19th century, they have been trained to harvest coconuts in Southeast Asia. They cause conflicts through crop-raiding (averaging 298 complaints annually in Malaysia), but also provide pest control services on plantations. They are sometimes hunted for food, kept as pets, and used in biomedical research. In local languages they are known as 'beruk' (Malay/Indonesian).
what_students_can_do: Support conservation organizations working in Southeast Asia
Study primate behavior and ecology in tropical forests
Promote sustainable agriculture practices including wildlife-friendly palm oil
Raise awareness about the wildlife trade issues affecting primates
Participate in ecotourism that supports local conservation
Learn about the importance of seed dispersal in forest ecosystems
fun_fact: Southern pig-tailed macaques are skilled rat hunters on oil palm plantations, killing as many as 3,000 rats per year as natural pest control
They have internal cheek pouches that can hold the same amount of food as their stomachs, allowing them to transport food hands-free
Unlike almost all other primates, these macaques actually love water and will readily enter it
In Thailand, they have been trained for over 400 years to harvest coconuts
Females are attracted to males with long canines, interpreting them as having 'good genes' to pass to offspring
